frequency_question: How often do final determinations by a federal regulatory body regarding an accreditor's status successfully meet strict formal revocation criteria rather than extension or renewal within the given window?
membership_rule: Includes any formal Department of Education review proceeding resulting in a final determination on recognition for a major professional or institutional accreditor over the past 30 years. Excludes voluntary relinquishments of accreditation authority.

cases.name: Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools (ACICS) - 2016

coverage_note: 4 major contested review instances identified where formal termination was formally petitioned or initiated.
known_gaps: Minor reviews of smaller accreditors that did not reach high-profile secretary-level final orders are excluded.
skeleton: Regulatory review cycles for recognized accreditors resulting in final adverse action versus renewal.
multiplier: 2 revocations out of 4 high-profile contested review cycles where termination was actively considered.
validity_reason: Administrative procedures for recognition under the Higher Education Act remain stable across this timeframe.
